findings.minimal_repair: Accepted as a deterministic removal of the proven trigger; if a PGlite suite ever fails under serial scheduling, that is a new defect to diagnose, not a reason to restore parallelism.
findings.observed: PGLITE asked for the actual cause to be established. The checkpoint honestly narrows it to parallel file scheduling (the failing suites pass alone and under serial scheduling; they failed only in the full parallel run) but does not distinguish CPU from memory pressure. The repair removes that variable (serial file execution, enforced by a report-level overlap check) rather than masking it; no timeout, retry, skip or reclassification was added, which is what the check prohibited.

findings.expected: A committed unit test for the overlap check.
findings.minimal_repair: Add the four cases to tests/architecture/gate-proof.test.ts in a small follow-up.
findings.observed: assertSerialSuiteReport has no committed test: tests/architecture/gate-proof.test.ts was not a write path of this task (the task definition omitted it). The reviewer exercised it directly at the frozen tree: serial and touching intervals accepted; overlapping (sorted and unsorted) and missing timing rejected with the expected messages.

The new teardown is a production write path (DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE). It is correctly bounded: only the two reserved names, found by exact match, quoted, under a verified admin role (rolbypassrls), pinned TLS, followed by a read-only zero-residue verification; failure blocks receipts. Recorded for awareness, not as a defect.

manual_checks.note: Matches the recorded failures and the owner-run read-only residue check (no scratch schemas).

Serialization via --no-file-parallelism, enforced by assertSerialSuiteReport so a bypass yields no receipts.
See N1: cause narrowed to parallel scheduling and removed; no prohibited masking.
